text:
maria: Quick sanity check — need to lock down ownership of 'mode translation' for Dedicated+Private sidecar flows. Who owns translation of client manifest into runtime config: control-plane or runtime adapter?
aj: my vote: control-plane owns policy decisions, runtime adapter owns local wiring. keeps control-plane simple.
devindra: worried about secret handling. if control-plane transforms manifests it will touch KMS/HSM wrappers. private deployments want minimal secret exposure.
sarah: agree w/ @devindra. for Private we should prefer a translation hook that runs inside customer VPC (sidecar) so secrets never leave. control-plane still declares high-level policy.
maria: ok, so split responsibilities: control-plane = policy/intent, sidecar/runtime = concrete credentials + env-specifics. but we need a clear interface.
aj: propose a compact handshake: control-plane sends a 'manifest-intent' blob + signatures; runtime exposes a small /apply endpoint that accepts intent and returns applied config + capability flags.
devindra: sample proto idea:
```
intent: { model: 'redwood-embed-1', quant: 'int8', routes: ['eu-west'], sso: true }
signature: '...'
```
runtime responds:
```
applied: true
capabilities: ['kv-cache', 'hw-quant']
secrets_consumed: ['kms:arn:..']
```
aj: that lets control-plane remain oblivious to secret contents; runtime reports capabilities for routing decisions.
sarah: important: runtime must assert it did not exfiltrate secrets — we need an attestation field (signed assertion) and audit entries. also must include latency footprint estimate for SLO routing.
maria: how to handle rollbacks/eviction? if runtime can't apply intent, it should provide a fallback manifest or explicit reject with reason. control-plane uses fallback policy.
aj: add a `fallback_policy` field on intent. control-plane can specify 'use-hosted-variant' or 'deny' or 'degrade-to-cpu'.
devindra: edge case: dedicated pools where runtime can't serve requested quantization. need a use-case doc for 'downgrade vs route-to-hosted'.
sarah: ops-bot: can we get a short retention policy + audit log export for attestation events?
ops-bot: DeploymentAuditBot: created export job audit/export/18299-apply-attest at 2026-04-02T12:40Z :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks. action items: 1) @aj draft handshake proto (intent, signature, fallback_policy, capability flags, latency estimate) 2) @devindra write secret-handling constraints & attestation requirements 3) @sarah draft audit retention + KMS integration notes. I'll collate into an RFC next week. :thumbsup:
